WoW: Forever · Crafting · Updated October 8, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70245 · Null Ossuary

Recipes, skill levels and reagents come from foreverchanges.pro's reading of the beta client and are solid. Professions are capped at skill 225 in the beta, so nothing above that has been crafted by anyone. The levelling route below is computed from recipe skill-colours rather than tested, and the source publishing it says so. Where the new herbs come from is unpublished.

Is Alchemy worth taking?

It is a money profession and a raid-utility profession. It earns Legacy Points at skill 150, 225 and 300, and grants a title. Of the crafting professions it has the strongest case (ours, not a source's).

It suits every class: the new consumable ladders cover spell healing, spell damage and attack power at every tier. Healers and casters gain the most, since the Mender's, Cleric's and Mageblood lines are all new (ours, not a source's).

What it pairs with

Alchemy eats herbs, and Herbalism is the only profession that gathers them. That is unchanged, and Alchemy has no other feed.

Our own reading, which no source publishes: the Herbalism half is more optional than it was. Merchant's Favor buys recipes, and the crates that earn it are tradeable, so you can buy them at the auction house.

What Forever added

Three new consumable ladders, spanning the whole level range:

LadderWhat it givesSkill range
Mender's PotionMender's PotionItemSpell healing, +13 up to +8830 → 280
Spellblasting PotionSpellblasting PotionItemSpell damage, +7 up to +4735 → 285
Frenzy PotionFrenzy PotionItemAttack power, +12 up to +8040 → 290

Plus new Mageblood (mana per 5 seconds) and Cleric's (healing done) elixir ladders, and new Spirit and Intellect tiers.

Four new raid flasks. Each sits at skill 300, lasts 2 hours and gives +60 Stamina. All four carry a clause vanilla never had:

FlaskExtra effect, in Mount Hyjal, Hyjal Summit and the Barrow Deeps only
Flask of Natural AccuracyFlask of Natural AccuracyItem5% hit chance
Flask of Natural AggressionFlask of Natural AggressionItem4% critical strike
Flask of Natural PrecisionFlask of Natural PrecisionItem5% reduced chance to be dodged or parried
Flask of Natural SwiftnessFlask of Natural SwiftnessItem5% haste

These are zone-scoped, and vanilla has no design pattern like it. Their reagents are the new herbs: Death Lotus, Demonsage and Marefoil. No gathering node is published for any of the three, and only Demonsage and Marefoil have a gathering spell in the client.

The five vanilla flasks are all present and unchanged.

Changes that will catch out a veteran

  • Six oils now yield 2 per craft instead of 1: Fire Oil, Shadow Oil, Frost Oil, Goblin Rocket Fuel, Ghost Dye and Stonescale Oil. If you are budgeting Stonescale for flasks off vanilla memory, you are buying twice what you need.
  • Reagents changed on several low-level recipes. Minor Mana PotionMinor Mana PotionItem now wants Peacebloom where it wanted Silverleaf; Elixir of Minor DefenseElixir of Minor DefenseItem wants one Silverleaf and one Peacebloom rather than two Silverleaf.
  • A new drawback mechanic. The Discolored Healing Potion line became five tiers, and they read: "Restores X health instantly, however you also suffer 75% of that amount over time."
  • Alchemy LaboratoryAlchemy LaboratoryItem at skill 300 is a workstation requirement: "needed for the most advanced Alchemy recipes." Nothing like it exists in vanilla.
  • There is no specialisation system. Elixir, Potion and Transmute Mastery are Burning Crusade. Do not go looking for them.
  • The Alchemists' StoneAlchemists' StoneSpell · PhysicalCastInstant is unchanged from vanilla, and still substitutes for a Philosopher's Stone.
  • No passive Alchemy bonus has been shown, and the claim that Forever makes elixirs and flasks last longer is false. The Legacy perk people cite, PermanencePermanenceTalentCastInstantYour class abilities which grant long-duration stat or attribute benefits to all party or raid members last 100% longer, and the benefits you gain from resting at a camp last 50% longer., covers class abilities and camp rest, not consumables.

Levelling it

The published route, computed from recipe costs rather than tested:

  1. 1 → 64: Elixir of Minor DefenseElixir of Minor DefenseItem, ~65 crafts
  2. 64 → 80: Minor Mana PotionMinor Mana PotionItem, ~21
  3. 80 → 96: Blackmouth OilBlackmouth OilItem, ~31. Keep them
  4. 96 → 100: Elixir of WisdomElixir of WisdomItem, ~4
  5. 100 → 130: Swim Speed PotionSwim Speed PotionItem, ~30
  6. 130 → 166: Fire OilFire OilItem, ~51. Keep them
  7. 166 → 175: Elixir of Fire PowerElixir of Fire PowerItem, ~11
  8. 175 → 190: Greater Discolored Healing PotionGreater Discolored Healing PotionItem, ~19
  9. 190 → 209: Great Rage PotionGreat Rage PotionItem, ~22. Vendor recipe
  10. 209 → 237: Nature Protection PotionNature Protection PotionItem, ~46. Vendor recipe
  11. 237 → 250: Draught of Detect UndeadDraught of Detect UndeadItem, ~14
  12. 250 → 260: Stonescale OilStonescale OilItem, ~30. Keep them
  13. 260 → 265: Draught of Detect DemonDraught of Detect DemonItem, ~5
  14. 265 → 295: Elixir of Greater DefenseElixir of Greater DefenseItem, ~34. Vendor recipe, and the expensive block
  15. 295 → 300: Major Mana PotionMajor Mana PotionItem, ~5

The beta wall lands mid-step 10, at skill 225. The longest single step is 209 to 237, and it needs a vendor recipe, so buy that before you get there.

Certification and title

New in Forever: an Alchemy Certification at skill 300 unlocks the title "the Alchemist". The title is account-wide, but only a character with 300 Alchemy can display it.

What is not known

Where Death Lotus, Demonsage and Marefoil are gathered. They are reagents in the new flasks and have no published node. Where Lich's Index Finger, the Alchemy Laboratory's reagent, comes from. Whether the Laboratory is needed to learn the top recipes or only to craft them. Whether transmute cooldowns changed. And whether the new flasks' Hyjal clause covers the raid tier opening December 9.
